_note: Each scene is a list of [spoken_text, pause_after_seconds]. 'spoken_text' spells numbers out so the TTS reads them the way a narrator would.

s1_hook: In September two thousand eight, one of the biggest investment banks in the world collapsed.
And it was only the beginning.
s2_problem: To understand why, we need to go back a few years.
American banks were handing out mortgages to people who could barely afford them.
s3_bigger_problem: But banks didn't just keep these mortgages.
They bundled thousands of them together into financial products called mortgage-backed securities,
then sold them to investors around the world.
s4_collapse: Suddenly, those supposedly valuable investments were worth far less than anyone expected.
And the losses spread throughout the global financial system.
s5_lehman: On September fifteenth, two thousand eight, Lehman Brothers filed for bankruptcy.
A one hundred fifty-eight-year-old financial institution was gone.
It was the largest bankruptcy in American history at the time.
s6_aftermath: Millions lost their jobs and homes.
Governments had to step in to stop the financial system from collapsing completely.
s7_final: But perhaps the most frightening part?
The entire crisis was built on one assumption:
that house prices would never fall.
